2026-11-22.title: Sunday of the Annunciation to Mary, Mother of God
readings: The first promise: the woman and her offspring
Not by might, but by my Spirit
O that you would tear open the heavens and come down
We are called children of God
God sent his Son, born of a woman
The angel Gabriel is sent to Mary
2026-11-22.verse: Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.
theo: Last Sunday the angel came to an old priest in the Temple. Today the same angel, Gabriel, comes to a young virgin in Nazareth, a village never mentioned in the Old Testament. God's greatest work begins in a hidden house, in the heart of a woman who listens.

The readings stretch from the first pages of the Bible to its fulfilment. In the garden, after the first sin, God promises that the offspring of the woman will strike the serpent's head (Genesis 3:15). Isaiah cries: “O that you would tear open the heavens and come down” (Isaiah 64:1). St Paul answers: “When the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman” (Galatians 4:4). The Annunciation is the moment when heaven opens and God comes down.

“The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore the child to be born will be holy; he will be called Son of God.” Mary conceives not by human power but by the Spirit, as Zechariah's vision promised: “Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit” (Zechariah 4:6). Her child is truly God and truly man; that is why the Church calls her Theotokos, Mother of God.

Zechariah asked, “How will I know?” and was silenced. Mary asks, “How can this be?” and then gives her free consent: “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.” The Fathers saw in her obedience the reversal of Eve's disobedience. Through her “yes”, the Son of God becomes our brother, and we become “children of God; and that is what we are” (1 John 3:1).
conn: In Genesis 3 a woman listens to the serpent and humanity falls; in Luke 1 a woman listens to the angel and salvation enters the world. Genesis 3:15 is called the “first Gospel”.
The evening Gospel (Matthew 1:1–17) lists sinners and saints, foreigners and kings. God's promise travels through a real, untidy family history to Mary, “of whom Jesus was born”.
The word Luke uses recalls the cloud that covered the Tabernacle (Exodus 40:35). Mary becomes the dwelling place of God.
“Nothing will be impossible with God” (Luke 1:37) echoes the Lord's words to Abraham about Sarah: “Is anything too wonderful for the LORD?” (Genesis 18:14).
altar: At the epiclesis of the Holy Qurbono the priest calls the Holy Spirit upon the bread and wine, as the Spirit came upon Mary. The same Lord who took flesh in her womb becomes present on the altar. Mary's “let it be with me” is the best preparation for Holy Communion.
outline: Contrast: an angel in the Temple to a priest (last week); an angel in a village house to a girl (today).
Genesis 3:15 to Galatians 4:4: God never forgot his first promise.
“Not by might, nor by power.” Christ comes by the Spirit's power, not by human means. Mary is truly Mother of God.
Point 3 · Mary's question and Mary's yes
Faith may ask questions; it ends in surrender. Compare Zechariah.
Where is God asking for my yes this week: a vocation, a forgiveness, a hidden duty?
“Here am I, Lord; let it be with me according to your word.”
live: Pray the Angelus at noon every day this week; in the family, at least once together.
Say yes to one hidden duty
Do one task you have been avoiding at home or at work, quietly, as your “let it be”.
Pray one decade of the Rosary each evening, meditating on the Annunciation.
fathers: “The knot of Eve's disobedience was loosed by the obedience of Mary; what the virgin Eve bound through unbelief, the Virgin Mary set free through faith” (Against Heresies III, 22, 4).
He imagines the whole world waiting for Mary's reply: Adam, Abraham, David and all the fathers beg her to answer the angel quickly and give her consent (Homilies in Praise of the Virgin Mother 4, 8).
magis: Mary was not a merely passive instrument but cooperated in human salvation by free faith and obedience; the Fathers compare her with Eve: “death through Eve, life through Mary”.
Mary, “full of grace”, was prepared by God; she is truly Mother of God (Theotokos) because she is the mother of the eternal Son made man.
At the Annunciation Mary entrusted herself to God completely, with the “obedience of faith”, responding with all her human and feminine “I”.
saints: 23 Nov: St Clement of Rome, Pope and Martyr. 25 Nov: St Catherine of Alexandria. 29 Nov: St Jacob of Serugh (Mar Jacob of Sarug), great Syriac poet (falls on Sunday in 2026). Confirm in the 2026–27 lectionary.
2026-11-22.prayer: Lord God, you sent your angel to the Virgin Mary, and by the power of the Holy Spirit your Son took flesh in her womb. Give us her listening heart and her generous “yes”, that Christ may be formed in us. Through her prayers, Mother of God, keep us faithful. Amen.

quick: God keeps the first promise made in Eden.
By the Holy Spirit the Son of God becomes man in Mary, Mother of God.
Mary's “let it be” undoes Eve's “no”, and invites ours.
2026-11-22.action: Pray the Angelus at noon every day this week.
2026-11-22.question: Where is God asking for my “yes” this week?
2026-11-22.special: Second Sunday of Suboro: the Annunciation to the Blessed Virgin Mary.
illus: When a bride and groom say “I do” at the altar, two short words change two whole lives. Mary's “let it be” was even shorter, and it changed the history of the world.

family.explain: God sent the angel Gabriel to Mary. She said yes to God, and Jesus, God's Son, became a little baby in her womb.
family.intention: We pray that each of us may say yes to God like Mary.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing God wants me to say yes to this week?”

catechism: Mary's “Fiat” and the obedience of faith.
kidsaint: His name means “God is my strength”. He brought God's messages to Daniel, to Zechariah and to Mary. Lesson: listen carefully when God speaks to you in prayer and through your parents and teachers.
term: Greek for “God-bearer”. The Council of Ephesus (431) taught that Mary is truly Mother of God, because the child she bore is the eternal Son of God made man. In the Syriac tradition she is called Yoldath Aloho.
termMore: A prayer recalling the Annunciation, traditionally said at morning, noon and evening when the church bell rings: “The angel of the Lord declared unto Mary…”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, last Sunday an angel came to an old priest in the great Temple of Jerusalem. Today the same angel goes to a little village called Nazareth, to a young girl named Mary. God's greatest work begins in a small house, in a heart that listens.

Our readings remind us that God had promised this from the very beginning. When Adam and Eve sinned, God said that the offspring of the woman would crush the serpent's head. For centuries the prophets cried, “O that you would tear open the heavens and come down!” And St Paul says, “When the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman.” Today that fullness arrives.

Mary asks a question: “How can this be?” Faith may ask questions. But then she says the words that changed the world: “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.” The Fathers said: Eve's disobedience tied a knot; Mary's obedience untied it. Through her, the Son of God became man; that is why we call her Mother of God.

God is still looking for hearts that say yes. Perhaps he asks you to forgive someone, to accept an illness, to give time to prayer, or to answer a call to the priesthood or religious life. In a few moments the Holy Spirit will come down upon this altar as he came upon Mary. Let us say with her: “Let it be with me according to your word.” Amen.
kids: Children, who visited Mary in her little house? The angel Gabriel! He said: “Mary, God is with you. You will have a baby, and you will call him Jesus.”
Mary said: “Yes, I will do what God wants.” And Jesus, God's own Son, became a tiny baby inside her.
Every day God asks us small things: to obey, to share, to pray. Let's say like Mary: “Yes, God!”

intro: Theme: “Let it be with me according to your word.”
Today heaven and earth meet in a small house in Nazareth. God's plan, promised from the first pages of the Bible, waits for the free “yes” of a young woman.

sub: After the first sin God promised a woman whose offspring would crush the serpent.
Through the centuries the prophets cried: “O that you would tear open the heavens and come down!”
In the fullness of time God sent his Son, born of a woman: Mary is that woman.
q: I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; he will strike your head, and you will strike his heel.
But when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the law.
points.apply: Thank God this week that he did not abandon humanity after sin.

points.h: Full of grace, by the power of the Spirit
sub: The angel greets Mary as the “favored one”: God's grace has prepared her.
The Incarnation is not human achievement but the work of the Holy Spirit overshadowing her.
God still works “not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit”.
q: Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, says the LORD of hosts.
The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore the child to be born will be holy; he will be called Son of God.
points.apply: Before every important task, pray: “Come, Holy Spirit.”

sub: Mary asks how, not whether: her question seeks understanding, not proof.
She surrenders like clay to the potter: “Here am I, the servant of the Lord.”
Her “yes” changes history; our small daily “yes” lets Christ be born in our world.
q: Yet, O LORD, you are our Father; we are the clay, and you are our potter; we are all the work of your hand.
Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.
points.apply: Pray the Angelus (or three Hail Marys) every day this week, morning, noon and evening.

concl: God never forces his love; he asks. In Mary humanity answered “yes” on behalf of us all.
Let us learn from her to listen, to ask, and to say each day: “Let it be with me according to your word.”
2026-11-22.resolve: Say one hidden “yes” to God this week in something you have been resisting.
